symptom: `mxcli playwright check http://frontend.local:8180/ -p app.mpr --role R` failed every run with `FAIL   the sign-in form is showing, not the page (pass --user/--password or --role)` after printing `login …`, while the same command without the URL passed; the login demonstrably happened (LastLogin advanced). When the session cap was then hit, `login failed` printed no explanation, because `playwright check` never passed RuntimeLogPath to the login
cause: RunPageCheck signed in on opts.BaseURL — with -p that is the run handshake's `http://localhost:<port>` — and then loaded the page on whatever host the URL named. The session cookies were set for localhost and the browser sent none to frontend.local, so the client started anonymous (`[Startup] … 401`) and drew the sign-in form. With a saved session the renewal path signed in again on localhost and retried, so every run added one live session
file: cmd/mxcli/docker/pagecheck_check.go (RunPageCheck → groupByOrigin/checkOrigin, RuntimeLogPath default), cmd/mxcli/docker/screenshot_login.go (SignOut), cmd/mxcli/cmd_playwright.go (--sign-out)
insight: The tell was in the two commands' only difference: project mode probes the base URL itself, an explicit URL may name another host for the same app. Cookies belong to a host, not to an app, so 'signed in' is a property of (host, session), and any check that signs in on one URL and probes another must derive the sign-in origin from the page. Cheapest repro needs no /etc/hosts: `run --local` prints `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/` while the handshake says localhost, so pasting the boot URL into `playwright check -p` fails the same way. Count sessions rather than trusting the verdict: the M2EE `runtime_statistics` action lists `user_sessions` per user — three failing runs, three sessions; four fixed runs, one; at six the trial cap refused the sign-in. Wrong turn to skip: the `[Startup] … 401` line is not the cause (it is the client's anonymous start, present on passing runs too), and the cap was not the cause either (reporter ruled it out) — it was the consequence. Sibling not fixed: a /p/ page the role may not open lands on `/login.html?messageCode=403#/…` and is reported as 'the sign-in form is showing (pass --user/--password or --role)' although the user is signed in; such a session is now signed out rather than re-signed-in beside every run
